questions.question: Why does the project wrap each plan in `<article>` rather than a generic `<div>`?
options: article elements render faster than div elements
Each card is independently meaningful content that would still make sense on its own — the semantic test article is designed for
div elements cannot be styled with Flexbox
It has no real effect, either tag would be equally correct
questions.explanation: article is for self-contained content; a pricing card describing one complete plan fits that definition, which is why it's chosen over a meaningless div.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of defining colors and spacing as CSS custom properties on `:root` instead of hard-coding values in each selector?
options: Custom properties make CSS parse faster in the browser
A single change at :root (e.g. a new brand color) updates every selector that references the variable, instead of requiring a find-and-replace
They are required for Flexbox to work
They only work in combination with Sass
questions.explanation: Custom properties centralize values so theming changes (rebrands, dark mode) touch one place instead of scattering edits across the stylesheet.

questions.question: Why is `flex: 1` applied to `.plan__features` inside each flex-column card?
options: So the features list grows to fill available space, pushing the CTA button to the same bottom position across cards even when feature lists differ in length
It's required for any list element
questions.explanation: Without flex: 1, cards with shorter feature lists would have their CTA button sitting higher up than cards with longer lists — a common layout-alignment problem Flexbox solves well.

questions.question: Why does the responsive CSS define `.pricing__grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }` as the default, only switching to 3 columns inside a `min-width` media query?
options: Because three columns are impossible on any screen size
This is the mobile-first approach: the simple single-column layout is the unconditional default, and larger screens opt into more columns as space allows
min-width media queries only work with one column
It's a typo and should be the other way around
questions.explanation: Mobile-first CSS starts from the simplest, most constrained layout and progressively adds complexity as more viewport width becomes available, rather than starting wide and cramming down.
